- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or mixed (0.0), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 7-day average is >10% above 30-day average, adjust forecast downward by 1–3%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1,0,-1,1), model misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not just historical mean.
